A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same temperature-scaling and conformal-prediction study by the same authors. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite the revised title and expanded scope.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments with LAC, APS, and RAPS on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet, including prediction-set sizes, coverage measurements, and temperature sweeps in Section 3 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on the same datasets, expanded sensitivity analyses, and an empirical comparison of ordinary and interpolated RAPS in Appendix C.

M1.justification: v1 recommends applying adaptive CP before or after undoing TS calibration. v2 introduces separate calibration and CP branches with independently chosen temperatures, plus optional interpolation of CP thresholds from anchor temperatures. Section 3.3 and Appendix C therefore add a substantive temperature-selection and deployment procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same image-classification datasets: CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet. The additional experiments vary temperatures, sample allocations, and coverage targets within this retained coverage; they introduce no new dataset, population, or task.

E2.justification: The main LAC, APS, and RAPS comparison set is retained. Appendix C and Figure 18 add a direct comparison between interpolated RAPS and ordinary RAPS using computed thresholds, providing a limited additional comparison for the new procedure.

E3.justification: The reported TS calibration allocation changes from 20% to 10%; CP allocations expand from 20% to 5%, 10%, and 20%, with 10% becoming the default. v2 adds alpha = 0.05, extends the temperature sweep from 1–2 to 0.3–2, and replaces raw marginal and minimum-class coverage with MarCovGap and TopCovGap. Appendix C adds a small-data interpolation evaluation.

E4.justification: v2 retains the per-sample set-size and ECE-versus-NLL analyses, while adding sensitivity to CP-set size and coverage targets, class-coverage temperature sweeps, and an extreme-low-temperature failure analysis. Appendix C additionally tests threshold interpolation and whether small calibration sets recover useful trade-off curves.

E5.justification: Both versions retain median-of-means reporting over 100 random-split trials for the main experiments. Appendix C newly reports three separate single-trial realizations of the interpolation comparison. This adds run-level reporting without establishing an increase in repetitions of the existing experiments; confidence intervals and significance tests are not added.

E6.justification: v1 Table 1's set-size values reappear in v2 Table 5. v2 adds results for new splits, coverage targets, coverage-gap metrics, low temperatures, and interpolation. Its default CIFAR-100/ResNet50 APS sizes are 5.31 before TS and 9.14 after TS under revised settings, so these are not same-setting gains over v1. The NLL-optimal temperature entry also changes from 1.338 in v1 Table 4 to 1.438 in v2 Table 3.

T1.justification: Most propositions and proofs are retained. Appendix B.4 revises the mathematical coverage measures, notably replacing minimum-class coverage with the average absolute gap among the worst 5% of classes. Corollary 4.3/A.3 loses its explicit nonrandomized restriction without corresponding randomized-score reasoning. Theorem 4.4's small-step formulation largely restates the earlier ascent-direction result.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion shift from emphasizing TS's detrimental set-size effect and recommending its avoidance to claiming a useful size–class-coverage trade-off. v2 adds practitioner guidance for choosing separate temperatures and combining adaptive CP with calibration as a central contribution.

C2.justification: v1 treats improved conditional coverage as a relatively minor benefit. v2 makes competing size and coverage objectives central to its interpretation and explains why temperature choice depends on user requirements. It adds substantive limitations concerning unknown metric-versus-temperature curves, numerical breakdown at extremely low temperatures, and interpolation sensitivity when thresholds approach one.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands previously sparse implementation documentation. Appendices B.1–B.2 identify the pretrained ImageNet model source, CIFAR training settings including 300 epochs and SGD hyperparameters, GPU hardware, and approximate experiment runtime. Appendix C specifies a degree-five interpolating polynomial and six anchor temperatures. These are disclosures and new-procedure details, not evidence that retained classifiers were retrained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to prior TS-plus-CP applications, conditional-coverage limitations, and class-conditional evaluation, including Lu, Gibbs, Vovk, Barber, and Ding works absent from v1. It refines the positioning by distinguishing the few CP studies using calibration from the majority that do not, while retaining the claimed gap concerning TS's effects.

P1.justification: The abstract, contributions, experimental discussion, and conclusion are substantially rewritten around the trade-off and practical guidance. Calibration-loss explanations move into the appendix, Appendix B is reorganized, and Appendix C is introduced. The title changes from 'On Calibration' to 'On Temperature Scaling.'

P2.justification: The main document changes from two columns to one with extensive reflow and repositioning. Separate size and threshold plots are combined with coverage plots in v2 Figure 3, coverage tables are reorganized, and new workflow, sensitivity, low-temperature, and interpolation displays are added. Existing reliability and per-sample plots are retained in reorganized locations.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves the justification and usefulness of the paper's main recommendation: it replaces v1's emphasis on avoiding TS with measured, task-dependent balancing of set size and class coverage. Sensitivity experiments, low-temperature failure analysis, practical validation in Appendix C, and training disclosures strengthen empirical grounding and reproducibility. These gains outweigh localized weaknesses: interpolation is demonstrated only on one dataset-model pair across three runs, and removing the corollary's nonrandomized qualification reduces theoretical precision.
